notes: Swimlane walk of the SIPOC's register-to-handoff segment, first drawn July 21, step times filled in August 3 from the time study's element medians (typical cycle, robust to the flagged July 28 rush outlier -- the sum of element medians, a typical cycle, not the mean total; the eight timed cycles average 8.8): 0.8 + 4.5 + 2.0 + 0.6 + 0.5 = 8.4 minutes -- the charter baseline. Demand block: weekday 7:00-10:00 peak (180 min, the peak window every other artifact in this demo uses); 48 espresso orders per peak (July tally, same count the spaghetti observation logged) -- pace 3.75 min per order. The engine's constraint readout (processing steps only -- value_add/enabling, matrix A-7 fidelity fix) names s3, Prepare drink at espresso station, 2.0 min, as the constraint -- it meets the 3.75 pace; the espresso-station lane carries 2.6 min of processing work across s3 and s4 (2.0 + 0.6). The engine's longest-step readout (any type, waits included) names s2, Cup waits in drink queue, 4.5 min -- honestly exceeding the 3.75 pace, but a pure wait can never be named the constraint: it sits downstream of the constraint, its consequence, not its cause.

Marked cups are WIP between register and machine -- nine deep during the July 28 8:12 rush

steps.reason: The transformation the customer pays for: dose, pull, steam, build

wastes.note: Grinder rework: 10 of the 40 tallied delays were re-pulls after sour or channelled shots (check sheet)
A grinder round trip per drink -- the grinder sits 2.3 m from the machine at the far end of the back counter (spaghetti route R2, 52 trips per peak)
